externalFindings.identity: Dutch-taught full-time VU Rechtsgeleerdheid, RIO 50700, OER effective 1 September 2026 and adopted 4 June 2026. No formal specialization is required. The current study guide and article 11.3 agree on the ordinary degree units. The transition notice is cohort-specific and does not replace article 11.3 for new students.
externalFindings.creditCoverage: 60+60+60 EC. First-year property and family law are each 3 EC. The ordinary third-year thesis and moot court count once each at 6 EC. Catalogue duplicates are parallel course codes. The OU bridging thesis, separately listed internship and honours are not required in addition. An open 30 EC block is real elective space.
externalFindings.progression: Article 9.1 links advanced administrative, contract, property, criminal and constitutional law and legal encyclopedia to their respective foundations, and European fundamental rights to both European and constitutional law foundations. The thesis assessment requires 120 EC including Legal Skills. Moot court requires 99 EC including Legal Skills. The illustrated sequence reaches both thresholds after two years.
externalFindings.additionalRequirements: Articles 10.4 and 11.3 integrate the Dutch language assessment and PPI 1 in Legal Skills, and PPI 2 in Administrative Law, without additive credits. Article 11.4 requires practical attendance by default, subject to the published course rules. Article 14 sets the positive first-year study advice at 42 EC.
externalFindings.electives: Articles 12.1 and 12.2 allow approved minors, faculty exchanges and coherent course packages. Exchange and coherent package conditions include at most 6 EC at level 100 and at least 12 EC at level 300. Eligible VU university minors and listed faculty minors can be taken without prior examination-board permission, subject to admission rules.
externalFindings.substance: Legal Skills includes legal problem-solving, drafting and oral argument. Moot court applies procedural context to written pleadings and oral advocacy. The thesis assesses sustained legal research and writing. The civil and insolvency procedure and formal criminal law course entries substantiate procedural depth beyond general dispute-resolution or crime content.

construction: The broad closest candidate tests all core legal interests, including legal research, through discipline-specific courses and complementary methods. A technology/climate direction is tested jointly because the common regulatory questions give it a coherent core. The legal-minor interest is a stable direction for choosing contextual courses and does not fix the 30 EC elective block. Examples and careers stay search-only.
